perspective:
Cynthia’s available information:

- I teach evening classes at the community center, and Christina is a colleague there who works with marketing.
- In a staff meeting about next semester’s marketing, I argued that we should highlight traditional classes because they have been the backbone of our success. I heard Christina say there is interest in more dynamic, interactive sessions, that we should showcase innovation, and that we could find a balance. I remained unconvinced and said our core audience values structure and depth.
- After seeing positive feedback from Christina’s last campaign, I began to doubt my earlier resistance. I asked her what she did differently. She told me she focused on interactive elements and social media to create conversation rather than just broadcasting information. I found it intriguing and said she had captured both depth and flash. She said blending the new with the old could help us learn from each other.
- Encouraged, I proposed a pilot project combining traditional lectures with interactive online sessions. Christina said she liked the idea and was excited to outline specifics. I hoped it would enhance learning and draw a wider audience.
- The pilot succeeded. I wanted to scale it up, said I would organize resources and set up a schedule, and met with Christina to discuss logistics. She said she would coordinate with the marketing team to promote it. I was excited about the impact.
- After successful implementation, I knew feedback was overwhelmingly positive. I prepared a presentation to showcase our success and advocate expanding the project to other centers. Christina offered help, said other centers could benefit, and said it was a pleasure seeing our ideas come to life successfully. I felt proud of what we achieved.
